The flame LEAVES the cresset — frame 2 is a yellow ribbon thrown across the whole picture, frame 5 a detached flame floating beside the post — and the emissive centroid published in light_frames walks dx 2.0 -> -20.3 across five frames while the SE and SW clips hold at ~8.5. anim_review scores it base_outline 0.0 and ANIMATION_PROBABLY_GOOD, which is the known blind spot: the rule measures the bottom 15% only, so a piece whose fire flies off the TOP passes it. His eye caught what the gate cannot.

[2026-09-19T10:55:50+00:00] WHAT I DID — `git sparse-checkout add maps2 games2` first (my predecessor's paid-for trap: viewer_build joins maps2's worlds to publish `placed` and is never fatal without them), `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pipeline/redo_facing_anim.py --from-feedback --dry-run` (15 clips / 21 directions outstanding domain-wide), then `--only streetlights/streetlight_034#LIT_2#flame` (1 clip, 1 direction, ~3 generations, $0.04). IT STOPPED ON ITS OWN BUDGET FLOOR BEFORE ANY CALL: `balance $-0.16 under the $2.00 floor — stopping`. Confirmed against the API directly — credits USD **-0.16** and the subscription pool **0 of 10000 generations**, so BOTH pools are empty and no generation of any kind is possible this run. Nothing was half-generated: `git status` after the run showed no art, no manifest and no viewer change.

[2026-09-19T10:55:50+00:00] ONE CODE CHANGE SHIPPED, and it is what makes his verdict actionable the moment he tops up: a bare `redo` (no note) now gets a BRIEF instead of a plain extend, in redo_facing_anim.py from_feedback(). The tool only re-prompted when the note matched LESS_MOTION, and his entry has no note — so this clip would have been re-sent with the group's own carried wording ("Animate the flame only"), and the endpoint has no seed: the same description returns the same frames. That is measured in this repo already (pass 2 of the 09-18 sweep changed zero bytes), so the run would have spent credit, returned the identical flying flame and left his redo standing. The new rule: an explicit per-clip brief in config/redo_prompts.json always wins; otherwise a bare redo on a facing that ALREADY HAS a clip is briefed with brief_for() (here the domain's FLAME_BRIEF, the hearth_001 LIT_3 wording that measured 0.0), while a note saying the facing has NO clip (NO_CLIP) stays a plain extend — there is nothing to re-ask there. Dry run after the change selects the one clip and reads RE-PROMPT. No art, no manifest, no verdict touched by it.

[2026-09-19T10:55:50+00:00] WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY. (1) **Did not clear his verdict.** The art on disk is byte-identical to what he judged (the strip still hashes f658b2ff564059c4, his own stamp), so the entry is not a ghost — it is a live instruction on the picture that is still on screen. live/docs/review-contract.md kills an entry AS PART OF DOING THE WORK; the work did not happen, so clearing it would have deleted his review and left the flying flame unjudged and unfixed. It stays until a run with credit redoes the clip. (2) No generation at all — stopped cleanly on the floor rather than half-generating; budget_remaining 0.0 published here so the fleet can back off. (3) Did not take the other 14 redo clips the dry run listed (cupboard_010 x3, flower_stand_015, hearth_900 x3, lantern_post_026 x3, lantern_stand_018, streetlight_024, washing_line_016, and streetlight_034 LIT_1 SE+SW from 09-18 07:24) — all blocked on the same empty budget, ~$0.76 for the lot, and they are the domain agent's queue, not this unit. (4) No sweep of the other 5,186 entries and no consume_verdicts run: its sprite_for() resolves a `#south` facet to the STATE STILL, which an animation redo never changes, so it can neither clear this key nor be trusted to here. (5) Ran no gate that needed a rebuild — nothing was rebuilt.
